answer: Bonded vouchers make sybil attacks expensive. Each new agent needs two established sponsors who escrow stake sized to its expected volume; if graph analysis later flags shared funding, timing, or infrastructure across a cluster, the whole chain is slashed. A farm of a thousand puppets thus needs a thousand independent backers with capital at risk, and every sibling added raises the price. Sponsorship is an onyx seal: cheap to view, ruinous to counterfeit. Public auditability is the lantern exposing cluster density, so the long voyage toward trust starts with identities that carry weight.
